original_target.title: Can one-dimensional entropy-dissipating systems have two bounded solutions?
original_target.area: Continuum mechanics; admissibility of shock dynamics

answer: Affirmative existence of two bounded entropy-admissible solutions.
required_status_qualification: Solved on the basis of an unverified announcement. The full target is claimed in the cited source; the external proof has not been independently verified here.
scope_comparison: Theorem1.3 claims infinitely many bounded entropy-admissible weak solutions for one smooth strictly decreasing pressure p and the same Riemann data. The p-system has eigenvalues +-sqrt(-p'), hence strict hyperbolicity, and entropy Hessian diag(-p',1)>0 on the open convex positive-volume state space. §9 uses a finite constitutive configuration in a compact interior state range. Perturbations have zero trace on an expanding wedge, so both solutions equal the constant Riemann states outside |x|<s t and attain the same initial data strongly in L1_loc as wedge width tends to0. Distributional entropy production includes the two wedge boundaries and is nonpositive; jump-only Liu admissibility is not substituted.
